role: Ash - AI/ML lead (Sage team), evidence-scored AI workflow audit of RC 115f698
summary: Audited every AI workflow in the clean RC checkout (C:/Users/Sage world/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/rc-115f698): Java Meera (session/credit/on-behalf/tool executors/internal controller), Python influora-ai (chat SSE + tool loop, prompt assembler/persona, Claude/Gemini/Sarvam providers, analyze_site, brand-safety, trendspark, trend_tag, creator_suggestion, voice, spend gate), TrendSpark n8n tagger, creator copilot headline filter, and the FE Meera UI (meera-api.ts, MeeraChatPanel, MeeraCopilotChat, useMeeraStream). Executed: influora-ai pytest (874 passed, 1 failed - a timing-flaky heartbeat test, confirmed flaky on rerun), offline evals (5 datasets PASS, 2 datasets NOT RUN -> exit 1), 670 AI-related Java tests on a scratch copy of the RC (BUILD SUCCESS), n8n tagger sync check (ALL PASS). The core safety architecture is sound and test-backed: model IDs are valid pinned ids (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929, claude-haiku-4-5-20251001, gemini-2.5-flash), no anyOf/oneOf/allOf in any tool schema (grep + test_tool_schema_anthropic_valid), money tools are excluded from the offered tool set AND scope-gated (OnBehalfTokenService.SCOPE_DEFAULT) AND role-gated in Spring, replayed history never produces native tool_use/tool_result blocks, untrusted text is delimiter-wrapped + angle-bracket-neutralised, truncated tool calls are never salvaged, and every provider-bound route has a spend gate. No P0/P1 AI defect was found. Main go-live risks are P2: (1) brand-safety GARM batches of 25 items against max_tokens=4096 and 30s read timeouts will truncate/time out (feature flag off by default), (2) the chat history is client-supplied and unbounded, and prod sets no per-workspace hard cap, so one workspace can exhaust the shared $15/day global ceiling and take Meera down for everyone, (3) Gemini calls have no timeout (declared timeouts never wired), (4) Meera's show_creators matches the niche against name/bio/city instead of categories, (5) there is no live-model evidence for any AI feature: 2 eval datasets have zero fixtures and brand-safety fixtures look hand-authored. Nothing here is runtime-verified against real providers; all model-quality claims are model-dependent and unproven.

questions.question: Are all pinned model IDs valid, and can an env override silently mis-price or break them?
questions.why_it_matters: A retired/invalid model id 404s every call; an env override to a pricier model under a cheaper price row lets the $15 ceiling authorise far more real spend.
questions.answer: Valid. CLAUDE_MODEL defaults to claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929, TRENDSPARK/TREND_TAG/CREATOR_COPILOT default to claude-haiku-4-5-20251001, GEMINI_MODEL is the hard-coded gemini-2.5-flash. Pricing is keyed by literal ids and unknown ids resolve to the most expensive rate (fail-safe over-estimate). Prod compose does not override CLAUDE_MODEL.

questions.question: Can Meera move money or launch a campaign on its own, directly or via prompt injection?
questions.why_it_matters: Commit-tier AI actions are the P0 class for an escrow/wallet product.
questions.answer: No, three independent layers: request_payment/confirm_launch are excluded from get_tool_schemas(); the per-turn on-behalf JWT carries SCOPE_DEFAULT (no money tools); Spring requires resolveForWorkspaceRequiringElevatedRoleAndScope on those routes. loop.py also declines deterministically if one is ever proposed. create_campaign only ever produces a DRAFT and never sets budget/dates/perReelRate/slotCap.

Tests: OnBehalfTokenServiceTest (9), RequestPaymentExecutorTest (5), ConfirmLaunchExecutorTest (9), tests/eval/test_prompt_injection.py all green.

questions.question: Is the chat history sent to Claude server-sourced and bounded?
questions.why_it_matters: Client-controlled history is both an injection surface and an unbounded token-cost surface on the shared daily ceiling.
questions.answer: No. Block C is taken verbatim from the request body `conversation`, with no turn or token cap anywhere; the FE sends every in-memory message on every turn. Forged assistant/tool turns are neutralised (wrapped as untrusted, never native tool blocks), so the injection risk is mitigated, but cost and size are not bounded. See ASH-02.
questions.evidence: influora-ai/app/routes/chat.py:613,621 body.get('conversation'); app/prompt/assembler.py build_block_c_messages (no length check); src/components/feature/meera/MeeraChatPanel.tsx:762-771; src/components/creator/MeeraCopilotChat.tsx:293-297; grep for any history/body cap in app/ -> none.
questions.remaining_uncertainty: The host nginx http-block client_max_body_size is not in the repo (the ai vhost sets none, so it defaults to 1m unless overridden).

questions.question: Are provider timeouts, retries and circuit breakers actually wired for every provider?
questions.why_it_matters: A hung provider call holds an SSE stream or a Spring request thread indefinitely.
questions.answer: Claude: yes (connect 3s/read 30s, SDK default retries, breaker). Sarvam: yes (httpx timeouts). Gemini: NO. genai.Client is built with only api_key, and ProviderTimeouts.gemini_connect/gemini_read are never referenced. claude_first_token (8s) is also declared but unused. See ASH-03.

questions.question: Will brand-safety GARM classification succeed for a real creator's recent media?
questions.why_it_matters: It feeds creator_scores.brand_safety_score / garm_flags shown to brands; a silent NULL for most creators makes the feature cosmetic.
questions.answer: Probably not for creators with more than about 10 recent posts. Java sends up to 25 items per call (RECENT_MEDIA_LIMIT=30); each item needs about 300-365 output tokens (10 flags, each with a rationale), so a 25-item batch needs about 8-9K tokens against max_tokens=4096. The call is non-streaming with a 30s read timeout on both sides. Any chunk failure NULLs the whole creator (fail-safe). The feature flag is off by default. See ASH-01.

questions.remaining_uncertainty: Not executed against the live model; the exact tokens per item and generation speed are model-dependent.

questions.question: Does a failed or blank AI turn refund the brand's AI credit, and does a successful turn keep it?
questions.why_it_matters: Billing brands for our own failures, or refunding delivered replies, are both money-path defects.
questions.answer: Mostly yes. The credit is charged at send (AICreditService.tryConsumeForTurn). chat.py refunds via release_turn_credit on provider failure, empty/truncated fallback and every pre-stream error path. A client disconnect keeps the charge. Spring refuses a refund once a write-back persisted. Gaps: an AuthError at chat.py:353-354 (e.g. expired 60s stream token) returns before release_early, and MeeraSessionService.doSendTurn is not atomic (see ASH-05).
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Frequency of stream-token expiry in the field is unknown.

questions.question: Can a single tenant exhaust the platform-wide AI budget?
questions.why_it_matters: The global ceiling blocks every brand and creator once hit; that is a platform-wide Meera outage.
questions.answer: Yes. AI_DAILY_SPEND_CEILING_USD=15.0 is global. The per-workspace hard cap (WORKSPACE_DAILY_HARD_CAP_USD) is opt-in and unset in the prod compose. The $3/day per-workspace cap is warning-only. Chat reserves only $0.02 x 6 per turn, while the real cost scales with the client-supplied history size.

findings.title: Brand-safety GARM batch of 25 items cannot fit max_tokens=4096 or the 30s read timeouts: whole creator degrades to NULL
findings.evidence: Java chunks recent media into 25-item calls (BrandSafetyScoreService.java:76 CHUNK_SIZE=25; ScoreCalculationJob.java:101 RECENT_MEDIA_LIMIT=30). Python forces one analyze_creator_content tool call whose schema requires, per item, all 10 GARM categories each with a rationale plus overall_rationale (app/tools/schemas.py:516-601; app/prompt/brand_safety.py). One recorded single-item output is 1,275 chars of JSON, about 330 tokens, so 25 items need about 8K output tokens while brand_safety_max_tokens=4096 (app/config.py). The call is non-streaming messages.create with a 30s read timeout (app/providers/claude.py:392-399, config.py ProviderTimeouts.claude_read=30.0) and Java's client timeout is also 30s (BrandSafetyAiProperties.java:23). complete_with_forced_tool never inspects stop_reason, so a max_tokens cut surfaces only as a count mismatch -> 502 malformed_classification (routes/brand_safety.py _validate_model_result). classifyInChunks then discards the entire creator (fail-safe). Evals test single items only, so the batch path is never measured. AI classification: model-dependent (output length and speed) and external-provider-dependent (latency); code-supported for the limits.
findings.location: influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/scoring/BrandSafetyScoreService.java:76,166-207; job/ScoreCalculationJob.java:101; config/BrandSafetyAiProperties.java:23; influora-ai/app/config.py (brand_safety_max_tokens=4096, claude_read=30.0); app/providers/claude.py:362-437; app/routes/brand_safety.py
findings.impact: When BRAND_SAFETY_SCORING_ENABLED=true, creators with more than about 10-12 recent posts (every active creator) get NULL brand_safety_score/garm_flags/content_sentiment on every run. Every failed call is still billed (usage is recorded) and trips the brand-safety circuit breaker after 5 failures.
findings.recommended_fix: Cut CHUNK_SIZE to about 5-8 (keep BRAND_SAFETY_MAX_ITEMS_PER_CALL in sync). Only require a rationale for non-floor flags. Size max_tokens from items x per-item budget, or stream the forced tool call. Raise the Python read timeout and the Java requestTimeoutSeconds above the worst-case generation time. Check response.stop_reason == 'max_tokens' in complete_with_forced_tool and log it as a distinct error.
findings.verification_required: Staging run with BRAND_SAFETY_SCORING_ENABLED=true against a creator with 30 media rows; capture usage.output_tokens, stop_reason and latency per chunk.
findings.reproduction: Enable the flag; seed a creator with 30 MediaMetric rows with captions; run ScoreCalculationJob; observe 'malformed_classification' or timeout in influora-ai logs and NULL creator_scores.brand_safety_score.

findings.title: Chat history is client-supplied and unbounded, and prod has no per-workspace hard cap: one workspace can exhaust the global AI ceiling
findings.evidence: chat.py takes `conversation` verbatim from the body (app/routes/chat.py:613,621) and assembler.build_block_c_messages replays every entry with no turn or token cap. Only Block A/B carry cache_control, so the history is re-sent uncached on every tool-loop iteration (up to TOOL_LOOP_MAX_ITERATIONS=6). The FE sends every in-memory message on every turn (MeeraChatPanel.tsx:762-771, MeeraCopilotChat.tsx:293-297). The spend reservation per turn is a fixed $0.02 x 6 (chat.py:486-499), not size-aware. The global ceiling AI_DAILY_SPEND_CEILING_USD=15.0 is shared by all tenants. WORKSPACE_DAILY_HARD_CAP_USD is opt-in (config.py:443-445, gate.py) and is NOT set in deploy/utho/docker-compose.utho.yml. The $3 workspace cap is warning-only (chat.py:919-927). The ai vhost (deploy/utho/nginx-ai-influora.conf) sets no client_max_body_size and Caddy's AI_DOMAIN block sets no request_body limit. Code-supported; cost impact is model/provider-pricing dependent.
findings.location: influora-ai/app/routes/chat.py:486-499,613,621; app/prompt/assembler.py build_block_c_messages; app/costs/gate.py; app/config.py:427-445; deploy/utho/docker-compose.utho.yml (influora-ai environment); src/components/feature/meera/MeeraChatPanel.tsx:762-771; src/components/creator/MeeraCopilotChat.tsx:293-297
findings.impact: Per-turn input cost grows linearly with conversation length (quadratic per conversation). A single brand or creator, by heavy use or by posting a padded `conversation` up to the proxy body limit (default 1 MB, about 250K tokens), can push the shared $15/day ceiling over. After that every brand and creator gets 503 AI_SPEND_CEILING_REACHED (Meera, analyze-site, voice, brand-safety) until UTC midnight. The brand is charged only 1 credit per turn regardless of the size.
findings.recommended_fix: Build Block C server-side from persisted ai_messages (Spring already stores them) with a last-N / token budget, and ignore client history, or at minimum cap turns and chars in chat.py. Set WORKSPACE_DAILY_HARD_CAP_USD in the prod compose. Put an explicit client_max_body_size (for example 64k) on the ai vhost. Add cache_control on the last replayed message so tool-loop iterations reuse the history prefix.
findings.verification_required: Unit test that a 500-turn conversation is truncated. Staging check that WORKSPACE_DAILY_HARD_CAP_USD blocks a workspace while others proceed.
affected_features: AI spend ceiling / availability for all AI routes
findings.reproduction: Static: POST /chat with a valid stream token and a conversation of N turns; the prompt contains all N (build_block_c_messages has no cap). No live reproduction performed (would spend real money).

findings.title: Gemini calls have no timeout (declared gemini_connect/gemini_read are never wired); claude_first_token is also unused
findings.evidence: GeminiProvider.__init__ builds genai.Client(api_key=settings.gemini_api_key) with no http_options/timeout (app/providers/gemini.py). grep for gemini_read|gemini_connect|claude_first_token in influora-ai/app returns only their declarations (app/config.py:173,176,177). Both classify_site (analyze_site, also the in-chat analyze_site tool) and cleanup_transcript (voice) await generate_content with no bound. The chat SSE loop keeps emitting ': ping' every 15s while a tool runs (chat.py:797-805), and useMeeraStream resets its 30s heartbeat on every frame (useMeeraStream.ts resetHeartbeat), so the browser never times out a hung analyze_site. Java's voice client times out at 10s (MeeraVoiceAiClient request-timeout default 10) while STT (billed) plus uncapped Gemini cleanup run on the Python side. Hang behaviour is external-provider-dependent.
findings.location: influora-ai/app/providers/gemini.py (GeminiProvider.__init__, classify_site, cleanup_transcript); app/config.py:172-177; app/routes/chat.py:797-805; src/hooks/useMeeraStream.ts:139-149; influora-api integration/ai/MeeraVoiceAiClient.java:98-125
findings.impact: A stalled Gemini request leaves a Meera turn spinning indefinitely (pings keep the UI alive) and holds the spend reservation until its TTL. On voice, Java gives up at 10s after Sarvam STT was already billed, and the user gets 'type it instead'.
findings.recommended_fix: Pass http_options=genai_types.HttpOptions(timeout=int(settings.timeouts.gemini_read*1000)) to genai.Client, or wrap calls in asyncio.wait_for. Bound the in-loop analyze_site with an overall deadline. Wire or delete claude_first_token.
findings.verification_required: Unit test with a Gemini stub that never returns, asserting classify_site returns ok=False within the timeout.

findings.title: Meera show_creators matches the niche against name/username/bio/city, never against creator categories
findings.evidence: ShowCreatorsExecutor.execute builds combine(nameSearch(niche), singleCity(city)). CreatorProfileSpecifications.nameSearch (lines 30-41) LIKE-matches lower(displayName|username|bio|city). hasCategories (line 69) exists but is not used. Results are sorted by totalFollowers and capped at 10. The discoverable()+not-suspended filter is correctly applied via combine() (line 180). No unit test for ShowCreatorsExecutor exists (it is only referenced by InfoBarrierTest and controller tests). The tool schema describes the input as 'niche' (schemas.py:93-103), and the persona instructs Meera to use this tool rather than answer from memory. Code-supported; the user-visible effect is also model-dependent (what string Claude passes as niche).
findings.impact: 'Find skincare creators in Mumbai' returns only creators whose name or bio contains 'skincare' (or whose city contains it), not creators categorised as skincare. Meera then confidently reports few or no creators, or surfaces keyword-stuffed bios, and the brand is misled by a tool result the persona treats as ground truth.
findings.recommended_fix: Map niche to hasCategories(List.of(niche)) OR nameSearch(niche), reusing the same category normalisation CreatorDiscoveryService uses, and add a ShowCreatorsExecutorTest covering a category-only match.
findings.verification_required: Integration test: creator with categoriesJson=['Skincare'] and a bio without the word must be returned for niche='skincare'.
findings.reproduction: Static trace: ShowCreatorsExecutor -> CreatorProfileSpecifications.nameSearch predicate list contains no categoriesJson predicate.

findings.title: @Transactional is inert on self-invoked protected methods in the Meera send-turn and create_campaign paths (non-atomic writes)
findings.evidence: MeeraSessionService.sendTurn calls idempotencyService.executeOnce(..., () -> doSendTurn(...)) (line 344), and doSendTurn is `@Transactional protected` (line 355): a self-invocation, so the proxy is bypassed. IdempotencyService.executeOnce (line 116/131) is not @Transactional. So AICreditService.tryConsumeForTurn commits in its own transaction, then the USER message save, conversation save, BrandContextAssembler.assemble and the token mints run without a surrounding transaction. CreateCampaignExecutor.execute -> executeOnce(() -> doExecute(...)) has the same shape: CampaignIntent is saved before the Campaign, and a Campaign save failure (for example an AI title > 300 chars, Campaign.title length=300; intent product_name default VARCHAR 255) leaves an orphan READY intent. Tests pass with mocked repositories (MeeraSessionServiceTest 30, CreateCampaignExecutorTest 13), which cannot observe transaction boundaries. Code-supported, not model-dependent (the title-length trigger is model-dependent).
findings.impact: If context assembly or JWT minting throws after the charge, the brand loses a credit with no stream token and no refund path (Python is never reached, so release_turn_credit is never called). A partial create_campaign leaves orphan campaign_intents rows.
findings.recommended_fix: Make the transactional unit a public method on a separate bean (or use TransactionTemplate inside the lambda), and refund the credit in a catch around the post-charge steps. Validate or truncate AI-supplied title/product_name lengths before saving.
findings.verification_required: @SpringBootTest against MySQL (Testcontainers) forcing OnBehalfTokenService.mint to throw after the charge; assert the credit is refunded or rolled back.
affected_features: Meera send turn / AI credit billing
findings.reproduction: Static: grep '@Transactional' above 'protected TurnResult doSendTurn' and the lambda call site at MeeraSessionService.java:344.

findings.title: No live-model quality evidence: 2 eval datasets have zero fixtures (runner exits 1), brand-safety fixtures appear hand-authored, and there is no Meera chat eval
findings.evidence: `PYTHONUTF8=1 python evals/run_eval.py --offline all` in the RC exits 1: brand_safety_garm, analyze_site_classify, analyze_site_extraction, trend_tag and template_recommendation PASS; outcome_recommendation reports 'NOT RUN - 0 of 15 case(s) executed' and campaign_performance 'NOT RUN - 0 of 10'. All 12 brand_safety_garm fixtures carry flag rationales 'No concern found in the caption.' (even for high-risk cases), and brand_safety_score values snap to 10/40/90/100, which is consistent with hand-written rather than recorded outputs; they store no model or usage metadata. Every case is a single caption, so the 25-item batch path (ASH-01) is never measured. No dataset covers Meera chat tool selection, the persona money rails, creator persona or trendspark phrasing. Model-dependent by definition.
findings.impact: Persona rails ('never quote a number calculate_budget did not return', 'a draft is never live', 'never invent creators') and GARM accuracy are unmeasured before go-live. Regressions from a prompt or model change would not be caught.

Add a multi-item brand-safety case and a Meera chat golden set (tool-choice plus rail assertions). Make the CI eval job fail on NOT RUN.

findings.title: Two SSE heartbeat tests are timing-flaky (intermittent red on the influora-ai suite)
findings.evidence: The full pytest run gave 874 passed, 1 failed: tests/routes/test_f02_f14_route_level.py::test_f14_the_heartbeat_is_actually_delivered_during_the_wait (assert 1 >= 3 pings). An earlier -x run instead failed tests/prompt/test_f14_f20_correctness.py::test_f14_a_slow_tool_still_delivers_its_result_after_several_heartbeats. Re-running both files 3 times gave '1 failed, 30 passed', '31 passed', '31 passed'. Both use 50ms heartbeats against asyncio.sleep windows, which are sensitive to Windows timer granularity and CPU load.
findings.impact: A red CI run that is not a real defect erodes trust in the gate (the heartbeat feature itself is covered and works in most runs).
findings.recommended_fix: Replace wall-clock sleeps with a controllable fake clock/event, or widen margins (for example heartbeat 0.05 against a 1.0s tool and assert pings >= 3).
findings.verification_required: Run the two files 20x in a loop; expect 0 failures.
findings.reproduction: for i in 1 2 3; do python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/routes/test_f02_f14_route_level.py tests/prompt/test_f14_f20_correctness.py; done

findings.title: Tool inputs are not validated for required fields before Spring writes; a JSON parse failure is forwarded as {}
findings.evidence: ClaudeProvider.stream_turn sets tool_input = {} when the accumulated input_json fails json.loads and still yields a tool_use event (app/providers/claude.py:230-239). loop.py forwards dict(tool_input) plus workspace_id to Spring (loop.py:462-473) with no required-field check against the schema. Anthropic tool use does not strictly enforce `required` in non-strict mode. CreateCampaignExecutor.doExecute does not require product_name/creator_count: with {} it creates a Campaign titled 'Draft campaign' with a generic description. The model can also send keys that are not in the schema (end_brand_name/end_brand_category are read by the executor but never offered). Model-dependent.
findings.impact: Occasional empty-shell draft campaigns created 'by Meera', and the persona then narrates a draft that has no content.
findings.recommended_fix: Treat a tool_use whose JSON fails to parse like a truncation (never forward it). Validate required fields per schema in loop.py before forwarding and return an is_error tool_result so Claude can retry. Have CreateCampaignExecutor reject a missing product_name with 400.
findings.verification_required: Unit test: stream_turn with malformed partial_json must not produce a forwarded create_campaign.

findings.title: The model-reported brand_safety_score is not reconciled with its own garm_flags; duplicate categories are accepted
findings.evidence: _validate_model_result (app/routes/brand_safety.py) checks that the flag category set equals all 10 categories (set comparison, so duplicate entries with conflicting risks pass) and that the score is between 0 and 100, but never checks that a 'high'/'medium' flag lowers the score. Java picks the item with the lowest brand_safety_score as the creator-level score (BrandSafetyScoreService.java:231-249), so an item flagged 'high' but self-scored 95 does not pull the creator down. Model-dependent (a hallucination or inconsistency control is missing).
findings.impact: An inconsistent model output can certify unsafe content as safe at the creator level.
findings.recommended_fix: Derive brand_safety_score deterministically from the max flag risk (for example floor=100, low=90, medium=40, high=10), or reject outputs whose score is inconsistent with the max risk. Reject duplicate categories.
findings.verification_required: Unit test feeding a tool_input with a 'high' flag and score 95 expects rejection or recomputation.

findings.title: APPROVED_LLM_REGIONS is declared but never enforced; creator earnings and private rate floors are sent to Anthropic's default endpoint
findings.evidence: app/config.py:165 APPROVED_LLM_REGIONS=('asia-south1','ap-south-1','in') has no other reference in app/ (grep). anthropic.AsyncAnthropic is built with the default base URL (providers/claude.py:116). build_block_b_creator renders display/first name, city, tier, deal counts, total earned INR and PRIVATE rate floors into the system prompt (assembler.py). Voice audio goes to api.sarvam.ai and transcripts to Gemini. Mitigations present: the creator DPDP consent gate (chat.py:577, voice.py _creator_consent_gate) and allow-lists that strip PAN/GSTIN/bank/UPI. External-provider-dependent (data processing location).
findings.location: influora-ai/app/config.py:165; app/providers/claude.py:116-124; app/prompt/assembler.py build_block_b_creator; app/providers/gemini.py; app/providers/sarvam.py:28
findings.impact: A compliance posture implied by config (Indian regions) is not actually in force. Creator financial data leaves India on every creator turn.
findings.recommended_fix: Delete the constant or enforce it (for example a Bedrock/Vertex regional endpoint). Document the providers in the privacy notice and consent copy. Consider sending floors as bands instead of exact values.
findings.verification_required: Legal/DPO confirmation of the provider DPAs; an architectural decision on regional endpoints.

findings.title: Python auth rejections return FastAPI {detail:{...}}, which the FE stream hook cannot read; the auth-fail path also never refunds the send-time credit
findings.evidence: auth_error_to_http returns HTTPException(detail={'code','message'}) (app/auth/service_token.py:546-547), which is serialised as {'detail': {...}}. chat.py:353-354 raises it for any stream-token failure, and chat.py:432 does so for conversation_mismatch. useMeeraStream.ts:275-289 reads only payload.error.code/message, so the user sees the generic 'Stream rejected (HTTP 401)'. The credit for that turn was already charged at send (MeeraSessionService.doSendTurn); release_early is not reachable before verification (chat.py:347-354), so an expired 60s stream token (MeeraStreamProperties.streamTokenTtlSeconds=60) or a replay-guard rejection costs the brand a credit with no reply. Code-supported.
findings.impact: Opaque error copy, plus a lost credit on every auth-rejected turn (slow network or tab suspend between sendTurn and the stream open).
findings.recommended_fix: Register a FastAPI exception handler that emits {error:{code,message}} (or make the FE read detail.code). Have Spring expose a user-authenticated 'release unstarted turn' path (or a scheduled sweep of charged turns with no stream start) keyed by messageId.
findings.verification_required: Browser test: delay the stream open past 60s; observe the error copy and the credit balance.

findings.title: Spend reservations are taken before input validation on brand-safety and are not released on analyze_site no-usage failures (TTL-bounded leak)
findings.evidence: routes/brand_safety.py calls check_spend_gate(reserve_usd=...) before _validate_items, so a 400 (too_many_items, caption_too_long, and so on) returns without releasing gate.reservation. analyze_site.perform_site_analysis settles the reservation only inside `if result.usage:`; a provider error with no usage, an SSRF block, or an empty page returns without spend_tracker.release. Reservations expire by TTL (gate.py docstring), so the effect is temporary headroom loss on the global ceiling.
findings.impact: Under error storms, phantom reservations reduce the available daily ceiling until they expire, which can cause false AI_SPEND_CEILING_REACHED blocks.
findings.recommended_fix: Validate before reserving, and release the reservation in a finally block on every non-success exit.
findings.verification_required: Unit test asserting spend_tracker reserved total returns to 0 after a 400 and after an SSRF-blocked analyze.
